items.The study aims to analyze the impact of: 'Analyze' means study something closely; 'impact' means effect. The study wants to look at how social media changes things.
items.These factors significantly affect stude: 'Factors' are things that cause a result. These things change how well students do at school, a lot.
items.The researchers identified a clear relat: 'Variables' are things that change in a study. The researchers found the two things are clearly connected.
items.This approach is widely used in modern p: 'Approach' means a way of doing something. Many psychologists today use this way.
items.The theory is based on several key assum: 'Assumptions' are ideas people believe are true without proof. The theory starts from a few main ideas like this.
items.It is essential to evaluate the evidence: 'Essential' means very important; 'evaluate' means judge. You must check the proof with care.
items.The abstract gives a short summary of th: The 'abstract' is the short part at the start of a research paper that tells what the whole study is about.
items.Participants were randomly divided into: 'Participants' are the people in a study. They were put into two groups by chance.
items.Data were collected through online quest: 'Data' means information. The researchers got the information from online forms and by talking to people.
items.The findings suggest that sleep improves: 'Findings' are the results. The results show that sleep may help you remember things for a long time.
items.One limitation of this study is the smal: A 'limitation' is a weak point. A weak point of this study: it had only a few people.
items.Further research is needed to confirm th: We need more studies to be sure these results are correct. Writers often end papers with this sentence.
items.Dear Dr. Levi, I hope this email finds y: A polite way to start a formal email to a teacher: say hello and wish them well.
items.I am writing to ask about the assignment: Use this to say why you are writing: I want to ask when the work must be handed in.
items.Would it be possible to receive a short: A polite way to ask for a little more time to finish your work.
items.Unfortunately, I was unable to attend la: 'Unable to attend' means could not come. Sadly, I could not come to class last week.
items.I have attached a medical certificate fo: 'Attached' means added to the email. I added a doctor's note so you can see it.
items.Thank you for your time, and I look forw: A polite ending for an email: thank you, and I hope you will answer soon.
items.Today I'm going to talk about renewable: A way to start a talk by saying the topic: energy from sun and wind in Israel.
items.My presentation is divided into three ma: Use this to tell listeners the plan: my talk has three big sections.
items.As you can see in this slide, sales incr: Use this when you point to a slide: look here, the sales went up.
Use this to change to the next topic in a talk.
items.To sum up, the evidence supports our mai: 'To sum up' means to say it short at the end. The facts show our main idea is right.
items.Thank you for listening; are there any q: A polite way to end a talk and invite people to ask things.
items.However, the results were not statistica: 'However' means but. 'Not statistically significant' means the results could be by chance, so they do not prove much.
items.Furthermore, the method is cheaper and e: 'Furthermore' means also, adding a point. The method also costs less and is simpler.
items.These results may indicate a link betwee: 'May indicate' means maybe shows. These results maybe show that stress and sickness are connected.
items.It seems likely that the policy will be: 'It seems likely' means it will probably happen. The new rule will probably work.
items.Therefore, the hypothesis was only partl: 'Therefore' means so. So the idea was only part true.
items.In contrast, the second group showed no: 'In contrast' shows a difference. The other group did not get better.
items.The graph shows the number of students b: The picture with lines shows how many students there were from 2015 to 2025.
items.The number of applicants rose sharply in: 'Applicants' are people who ask to join. 'Rose sharply' means went up fast. Many more people asked in 2020.
items.Prices remained stable for most of the y: 'Remained stable' means stayed the same. Prices did not change much this year.
items.Unemployment fell gradually from eight t: 'Fell gradually' means went down slowly. Fewer people had no job: from 8% to 5%.
items.Women make up about sixty percent of the: 'Make up' means are part of. About 60% of the people in the group are women.
items.The table compares average salaries in f: The table shows the normal pay in five countries, side by side.
items.I always skim the text before reading it: 'Skim' means read fast to get the main idea. I read fast first, then slowly.
items.Underline the main idea in each paragrap: Draw a line under the most important idea of each part of the text.
items.Read all the answers before choosing the: Look at every choice before you pick the right one. A test tip.
items.If you don't know a word, guess from the: 'Context' means the words around a word. Use them to guess what a new word means.
items.Our study group meets in the library eve: A few students learn together at the library each Thursday.
items.I need to manage my time better before t: 'Finals' are the last big tests. I must plan my time better before them.
items.Yes, I'm a first-year student in compute: An answer to 'What do you study?': I am in my first year, learning about computers.
items.They're interesting, but the reading loa: An answer about classes: they are fun, but there is a lot to read.
items.I think it's next to the main library, o: An answer when someone asks where a place is: near the big library, on the first floor.
items.I'd love to; when and where do you usual: Saying yes to an invitation and asking about the time and place.
items.No, I share an apartment with two friend: An answer about where you live: I live with two friends close to the university.
items.I work part-time at a cafe and play bask: An answer about free time: I have a small job at a cafe, and I play basketball.

'I'd like' is a polite way to say 'I want'.

Say this when you want to pay at a restaurant.
items.Do you have this in medium?: Ask this when you need a different size: not small, not large.
items.Can I try it on?: Ask this when you want to put on clothes before you buy them.
'Too expensive' means it costs too much money.
Say this when a worker wants to help but you do not want to buy now.
items.Where is the fitting room?: The 'fitting room' is the small room where you put on clothes in a shop.
Say this when you decide to buy something.
items.Excuse me, where is the station?: A polite way to ask where the train or bus stop is.
The 'corner' is where two streets meet. Go to the right there.
items.Is it far from here?: Ask this to know if you must walk a long way.
'Next to' means right beside. It is beside the bank.
items.Where is the check-in?: 'Check-in' is the place where you give your bags and get your ticket for the plane.

Tell the worker you have one big bag for the plane.
Ask for a seat next to the plane's small window.

Say this at a hotel: I already asked for a room before.
items.What time is breakfast?: Ask when you can eat in the morning.

Say this when you want to leave the hotel and pay.
Say this when you feel sick.

items.Do you have something for a cold?: Ask if they have medicine for when you have a runny nose and cough.
items.How many times a day?: Ask how many times each day to take the medicine.
items.Where can I find the milk?: Ask a worker in which part of the shop the milk is.
Ask for a bag to carry the things you buy.
items.Is this on sale?: 'On sale' means cheaper than normal. Is this cheaper today?
items.Do you have fresh bread?: 'Fresh' means new and good, made today.
items.Can I pay with cash?: Ask if you can pay with paper money and coins.
items.Which bus goes to the city center?: Ask which bus number goes to the middle of the city.
Say this when you buy one ticket for the bus or train.
items.When is the next train?: Ask what time the train after this one comes.
items.Does this train stop at the airport?: Ask if the train goes to the airport on its way.
'Get off' means leave the bus or train. I want to leave at this stop.
items.How long does it take?: Ask how much time the trip needs.
items.Before I sign anything, I'd like to go t: 'Clause by clause' means one part at a time. I want to read every part of the contract before signing.
items.Would you knock a few hundred shekels of: 'Knock off' means make the price lower. Will you lower the rent if I stay two years?
items.Who is responsible for repairs if the bo: Ask who must fix things, like the water heater, if they break in winter.
items.I'd rather not hand over a blank check a: A 'blank check' is a signed check with no amount. I prefer not to give one as a promise.
items.Is there an early termination clause in: An 'early termination clause' lets you end the contract before its end date. Ask if there is one.
items.Had I known about the mold, I would neve: 'Had I known' means if I knew. If I knew about the mold, I would not have moved in.
items.I'd like to find out why I was charged a: 'Charged a fee' means asked to pay money. I want to know why I paid for a normal money transfer.
items.If I pay off the loan early, will there: 'Pay off' means pay all of it. A 'penalty' is extra money you must pay as punishment.
items.My account is overdrawn, and I'd like to: 'Overdrawn' means I took out more money than I had. I want to talk about borrowing for a short time.
items.We're trying to cut back on spending so: 'Cut back' means spend less; 'put money aside' means save. We want to save each month.
items.Could you walk me through the difference: 'Walk me through' means explain step by step. A fixed rate stays the same; a variable rate can change.
items.I didn't authorize this payment, so I'd: 'Authorize' means allow. 'Dispute' means say it is wrong. I did not allow this payment, so I object now.
items.I'm afraid this isn't what I ordered, an: 'I'm afraid' is a polite way to give bad news. 'Sorted out' means fixed. This is the wrong item; please fix it today.
items.I understand it's not your fault, but I': 'Passed from one department to another' means sent from person to person, and no one helped.
items.According to consumer protection law, I': 'Entitled to' means have the right to. The law says I can cancel in the first 14 days.
items.Store credit won't do me much good, so I: 'Store credit' is money you can spend only in that shop. I want my money back instead.
items.If the issue isn't resolved by Friday, I: 'Resolved' means fixed. 'Take it further' means complain to someone higher, maybe go to court.
items.Could you put that in writing so I have: Ask for a written copy of what you agreed, so you have proof.
items.I don't think we've been properly introd: 'Properly introduced' means formally told each other's names. I know the man getting married.
items.I'd love to stay longer, but I have to b: A polite way to leave a party: I want to stay, but I must wake up early.
items.You might have a point, although I see i: A polite way to disagree: you may be right, but I think a bit differently.
items.Sorry, your name has completely slipped: 'Slipped my mind' means I forgot. Sorry, I forgot your name; please tell me again.
items.We should get together sometime; I'll dr: 'Get together' means meet. 'Drop you a message' means send you a short note.
items.I'm not really one for big parties, but: 'Not one for' means I don't usually like. I don't like big parties, but this one was great.
items.I've been feeling run down for weeks, an: 'Run down' means tired and weak. 'Shake it off' means make it go away. I feel weak and can't get better.
items.Is there any chance of an earlier appoin: Ask if you can come sooner if another patient cancels.
items.Could you explain the side effects befor: 'Side effects' are bad things a medicine can cause. Please tell me before I start.
items.The pain comes and goes, but it gets wor: 'Comes and goes' means it stops and starts again. It hurts more when I lie in bed.
items.I'd like a referral to a specialist, jus: A 'referral' is a doctor's paper sending you to an expert. 'Rule out' means make sure it is not something.
items.Does my health fund cover this test, or: Ask if your health fund pays for the test, or if you must pay yourself.
items.From what I've read, the new policy is l: From what I read, the new rule will probably make homes cost even more.
items.I take headlines like that with a pinch: 'With a pinch of salt' means not fully believing. I don't believe such titles until I know more.
items.It's hard to tell whether the report is: 'Biased' means unfair to one side. It's hard to know if the report is unfair or just missing parts.
items.Whatever your political views, the risin: 'Whatever your views' means it doesn't matter what you think. Higher prices hurt all people.
items.I've stopped following the news so close: I stopped reading the news so much because it made me feel bad.
items.The minister's announcement raised more: The minister's news made people ask more than it explained.
items.I've already submitted this form twice,: I gave this paper two times already, and it seems they lost it both times.
items.Could you tell me exactly which document: Ask for the full list of papers you must bring next time.
items.I'd like to appeal the decision, since I: 'Appeal' means ask to change a decision. 'Miscalculated' means counted wrong. I think the tax is wrong.
items.The insurance company keeps asking for m: 'Paperwork' means forms and papers. 'Processing my claim' means dealing with my request for money.
items.Is it possible to handle this online, or: Ask if you can do this on the internet, or if you must go there.
items.If I'd filled in the form correctly the: If I filled in the form right the first time, I would have saved weeks.
items.Thanks for making the time; to be honest: 'Withdrawn' means quiet and not wanting to talk. Thank you for meeting; he seems quiet at home lately.
items.He hasn't said much, but I suspect he's: 'Struggling to fit in' means finding it hard to feel part of the group.
items.Would it be possible to seat him next to: Ask the teacher to put him beside a child who can help him feel welcome.
items.That sounds great; he really comes alive: 'Comes alive' means becomes happy and active. He loves having a real job to do.
items.His grandmother passed away in the summe: 'Passed away' means died. 'Hit him harder than he lets on' means he is more sad than he shows.
items.Definitely; in the meantime, please don': 'Don't hesitate' means please feel free. Write to me if anything happens.
items.I work as a nurse at a hospital in Haifa: An answer about your job: I take care of sick people at a hospital, mostly at night.
items.About three years now, and I really like: An answer to 'How long have you lived here?': three years, and I like that it's calm with many trees.
items.I usually go hiking with friends, and on: An answer about free time: I walk in nature with friends and see my parents on Saturday nights.
items.I grew up in a small town in the north,: 'Grew up' means lived as a child. I was a child in a small town, then moved for my studies.
items.Yes, I've been learning the guitar for a: I play guitar for one year now, but I don't play well yet.
items.Nice meeting you too, let me give you my: A friendly goodbye: I'll give you my phone number so we can talk again.
items.Yes, we booked a table for four under th: 'Booked' means saved before. We saved a table for four people at eight, name Cohen.
items.I think we're ready, but could you tell: Ask which food has no meat before you order.
items.Medium, please, and could I have a salad: An answer about how to cook meat: in the middle. And can I get salad, not fries?
items.Actually, I ordered the fish, but the wa: Tell the worker you got the wrong food: you asked for fish but got chicken.
items.Yes, please, but if it takes too long, I: Yes, but if I must wait a long time, I prefer not to get it.
items.No thanks, we're full, so could we just: We ate enough. 'The check' means the bill. We want to pay each for ourselves.
items.I'm looking for a warm winter jacket, pr: 'Waterproof' means water can't get in. I want a warm coat that is not heavy.
items.Usually a medium, but it depends on the: An answer about your size: often medium, but it changes, so I want to put it on first.
items.That sounds great, but do you have the s: I like it, but do you have the same one in a dark blue color?
items.I bought these shoes last week, but they: 'Return' means bring back to the shop. The shoes I bought are too small.
items.Yes, here it is, and the shoes are unwor: 'Unworn' means never used. Here is the receipt; the shoes are new and in the box.
items.I'd prefer a refund to my credit card, s: I want the money back on my card, because I didn't find anything else.
items.Sure, I have five years of experience in: An answer about your experience: I helped customers for five years at a big tech company.
items.I admire your products, and I'm looking: An answer to 'Why us?': I like what you make and want to keep learning here.
items.I'm very organized and calm under pressu: An answer about strengths: I plan well and stay calm when things are hard.
items.Once a client was very angry about a del: An answer about a hard moment: a customer was angry, so I called and fixed it.
items.I hope to lead a small team and take on: An answer about the future: I want to manage a small team and do more.
items.Yes, could you tell me what a typical da: Questions for the interviewer: what is a normal workday, and when will you choose?
items.Hi, I'd like to make an appointment with: Use this on the phone to ask for a time to see the doctor next week.
items.Unfortunately I'm at work then, so do yo: That time is bad because I'm working; do you have a later time?
items.Of course, my name is Dana Mizrahi, and: Of course, here is my name, and I'll say my family name letter by letter.
items.Yes, please ask her to call me back this: Please tell her to phone me today after 12 about the contract.
items.Sure, I said I need to move my appointme: I said I need to change my visit from Thursday to the next Monday.
items.No, that's everything, thanks, and could: That's all; please send me a phone message with the time.
items.We're thinking about renting a car and d: An answer about holiday plans: we want to rent a car and drive in north Italy for ten days.
items.Not yet, because prices keep changing, s: An answer to 'Did you book?': not yet; I'm waiting for a cheaper price.
items.I prefer an apartment, since we can cook: I like an apartment more, because we can make breakfast and it costs less for families.
items.I'd love to see the old town first, and: The 'old town' is the old part of a city. I want to see it, then eat lunch.
items.Probably our trip to Japan two years ago: An answer about your best trip: Japan two years ago, because of the food and people.
items.I'd love to, but let me check my schedul: 'Get back to you' means answer later. I want to, but I'll check my plans and tell you tomorrow.
items.I've had a bad headache and a sore throa: Tell the doctor your problem: my head and throat hurt for three days and it's worse now.
items.Yes, last night it was almost thirty-nin: Yes, last night my temperature was almost 39 degrees, so I couldn't sleep.
items.Only something for my blood pressure, wh: An answer about medicine: only a pill for my blood pressure, every morning.
items.I'm allergic to penicillin, so please do: 'Allergic' means my body reacts badly to it. Don't give me medicine with penicillin.
items.Should I take it before or after meals,: Ask if you take the medicine before or after eating, and if you can work.
items.Thank you, doctor, and could you also gi: A 'sick note' is a paper from the doctor saying you were too sick to work.
items.Yes, I have a reservation for three nigh: Say this at the front desk: I saved a room for three nights, with breakfast.
items.Thanks, and could you tell me what time: Ask when and where you can eat breakfast at the hotel.
items.Hi, the air conditioning in room 512 isn: Tell the hotel the machine that cools room 512 is broken and it's very hot.
items.I'd appreciate that, because this is the: 'I'd appreciate that' means thank you, please do. This is my second call about it.
items.Actually, the room is also very noisy at: The room is loud at night; can we change to a calmer room?
items.The staff were lovely, but because of th: The workers were nice, but the cooling was broken, so I want to pay less.
items.I don't think we've been formally introd: 'Formally introduced' means officially told names. 'Heading' means leading. I lead the data team.
items.Would you mind if I reached out next wee: 'Reach out' means contact. 'Synergies' means ways we can work well together.
items.A mutual colleague suggested I get in to: 'Mutual colleague' means a work friend we both know. They told me to contact you about growing your business.
items.I'd be happy to put you in touch with ou: 'Put you in touch' means connect you. I can connect you with the person who buys for our company.
items.What I find most rewarding about my role: 'Rewarding' means makes me feel good. I like turning numbers into plans most of all.
items.It was a pleasure meeting you; let's con: A polite goodbye at a business event: let's talk more over coffee later.
items.Let's make sure we stick to the agenda s: The 'agenda' is the list of topics. Let's talk only about these so we end on time.
items.Before we move on, does anyone have any: 'Raise concerns' means say worries. Before the next topic, does anyone have a problem?
items.I'm afraid we're running short on time,: 'Running short on time' means not much time left. 'Park that' means talk about it later.
items.Could you briefly bring everyone up to s: 'Bring up to speed' means tell the latest news. 'Where things stand' means the situation now.
items.To sum up, we've agreed to postpone the: 'Postpone' means move to later. In short, we will start next season, not now.
items.I'll circulate the minutes and action it: 'Circulate' means send to everyone. 'Minutes' are the notes of a meeting. I'll send them today.
items.I'm writing to follow up on my previous: 'Follow up' means write again about something. I'm writing again about the changed contract.
items.Please find attached the updated proposa: 'Find attached' means look at the file in this email. Here is the new offer to read and accept.
items.I'd appreciate it if you could get back: A polite way to ask: please answer me by Thursday after 12.
items.Apologies for the delayed response; I've: Sorry I answered late; I just came back from my holiday.
items.Could you kindly clarify whether the pri: 'Clarify' means make clear. Does the price include setting it up and help later?
items.Should you have any further questions, p: A polite email ending: if you want to ask more, please write to me.
items.Sorry, you cut out for a moment; could y: 'You cut out' means your voice stopped on the call. Please say the last part again.
items.I think you're on mute; we can see you b: 'On mute' means your sound is off. We see you, but we don't hear you.
items.Let me share my screen so everyone can s: 'Share my screen' means show my computer to everyone on the call.
items.My connection seems unstable, so I'll sw: My internet is weak, so I'll turn off my video for now.
items.Since we're in different time zones, let: 'Time zones' are areas with different clock times. Let's agree on hours when we all work.
items.I'll drop the link in the chat so you ca: 'Drop the link in the chat' means put the web address in the call's messages.
items.Would it be possible to push our meeting: 'Push back' means move to a later time. Can we meet Wednesday morning instead?
items.Realistically, we'll need at least two m: 'Realistically' means being honest about what's possible. We need two more weeks for testing.
items.I'm fully booked on Tuesday, but I could: 'Fully booked' means no free time. 'Squeeze in' means find a little time for.
items.Given the tight deadline, we may need to: 'Tight deadline' means little time. 'Prioritise' means do the most important things first.
items.Let's set a firm deadline and schedule a: A 'firm deadline' can't change. A 'check-in' is a short meeting to see progress.
items.If we fall behind schedule, I'll let you: 'Fall behind schedule' means be late. If we are late, I'll tell you early.
items.What are the main challenges your team i: Ask a customer what problems they have now with the company that sells to them.
items.I completely understand your concern abo: I understand you worry about money, so I'll tell you the choices.
items.Our solution typically pays for itself w: 'Pays for itself' means it saves as much money as it costs, here in six months.
items.Would you be interested in a free trial: Would you like to try it for free before you decide?
items.I'd like to check in and see how you're: 'Check in' means ask how things are. How is the new system going for you?
items.We can offer a ten percent discount if y: 'Commit to' means promise. We take off 10% if you sign for one full year.
items.I'd like to begin by giving you a brief: An 'overview' is a short general picture. I'll start with a quick look at the last three months.
items.As you can see from this chart, sales ro: Use this to point to a chart: sales went up fast in the second three months.
items.This figure is slightly misleading, so l: 'Misleading' means it may give the wrong idea. 'Put it into context' means explain the full picture.
items.Although revenue fell short of target, o: 'Fell short of target' means missed the goal. But we kept more money from each sale.
items.That's a great question, and I'll come b: A polite way to delay a question: good question; I'll answer it at the end.
items.To wrap up, I'd like to highlight three: 'To wrap up' means to finish. 'Takeaways' are the main things to remember.
items.I'm very sorry for the inconvenience, an: 'Inconvenience' means trouble. I'm sorry for the trouble; I'll check it now.
items.I can see why you'd be frustrated, and I: I understand why you are angry, and thank you for waiting.
items.Could you give me your order number so I: Ask for the order number to look at the information.
items.As a goodwill gesture, we'd like to offe: A 'goodwill gesture' is something kind you give to show you care. We will give all your money back.
items.I'll escalate this to our technical team: 'Escalate' means send to a higher level. I'll tell you news in two days.
items.Is there anything else I can help you wi: A polite way to end a service call: can I help with anything more?
items.I see where you're coming from, but that: 'I see where you're coming from' means I understand you. But it costs more than we can pay.
items.If you could extend the payment terms, w: 'Extend the payment terms' means give more time to pay. Then we might buy more.
items.Let's try to find a solution that genuin: Let's find an answer that is good for both of us.
items.Would you be willing to meet us halfway: 'Meet us halfway' means each side pays half. Will you share the delivery costs?
items.I'm afraid that's not something we can a: A polite way to say no: we can't accept that now.
items.Before we finalise anything, I need to r: 'Finalise' means make final. 'Run by' means show to check. Our lawyers must check first.
items.I'm a project manager with six years in: An introduction: I manage projects in tech for six years, and I love growing products.
items.I used to take on too much myself, but I: An answer about a weakness: I did too much alone, but now I give tasks to my team.
items.I raised my concerns privately, backed t: An answer about disagreement: I spoke privately, showed numbers, and we found a middle way.
items.I rank tasks by impact and urgency, flag: An answer about priorities: I do the most important and urgent things first and warn early.
items.I've grown a lot there, but I'm now look: An answer to 'Why leave?': I learned a lot, but I want more duties in a global company.
items.Based on my research and experience, I'm: An answer about pay: I'm hoping for about 25,000 shekels.
items.I was on the fence about the job offer,: 'On the fence' means not able to decide. I couldn't decide about the job, but now I have.
items.Let's not beat around the bush; the proj: 'Beat around the bush' means avoid saying something directly. Let's be honest: the project is late and costs too much.
items.Moving to Haifa was a blessing in disgui: 'A blessing in disguise' means something bad that later turns out good.
items.She's been under the weather all week, s: 'Under the weather' means a bit sick. 'Breathing room' means space and time. Let's not push her.
items.Don't jump to conclusions until you've h: 'Jump to conclusions' means decide too fast. Wait until you hear everything.
items.After months of arguing, we finally agre: 'Bury the hatchet' means stop fighting and be friends again.
items.Could you look into the billing issue an: 'Look into' means check. 'Get back to me' means answer me. Check the bill problem and tell me by Thursday.
items.We need to iron out a few details before: 'Iron out' means fix small problems. We must fix a few details before signing.
items.The meeting was called off at the last m: 'Called off' means canceled. 'Fell ill' means got sick.
items.I'll fill in for Dana while she's on mat: 'Fill in for' means do someone's job for a short time. I'll do Dana's job while she's with her new baby.
items.Management has decided to phase out the: 'Phase out' means stop using slowly. The company will stop using the old program this year.
items.If we cut back on travel expenses, we ca: 'Cut back on' means spend less on. 'Lay off' means fire workers. Spending less helps keep all jobs.
items.As far as I'm concerned, the proposal ra: 'As far as I'm concerned' means in my opinion. The plan makes people ask more than it explains.
items.I take your point, but I'm not entirely: 'I take your point' means I understand you. 'Add up' means make sense. I'm not sure the numbers are right.
items.With all due respect, I think you're ove: 'With all due respect' is a polite way to disagree. 'Overlooking' means not seeing. You forget the future costs.
items.I'd go so far as to say that this decisi: 'Go so far as to say' means say strongly. 'Backfire' means have the opposite, bad result.
items.That's a fair argument, although I'd see: A polite way to disagree: that's a good point, but I think a bit differently.
items.Not only is the plan expensive, but it's: 'Not only... but also' adds a second point: the plan costs a lot and also won't work.
items.Had I known how addictive the app was, I: 'Had I known' means if I knew. 'Addictive' means hard to stop using. I would not have gotten the app.
items.Smartphones have blurred the line betwee: 'Blurred the line' means made the difference unclear. Phones mix work time and home time.
items.It is widely believed that algorithms sh: Many people think computer programs change what we believe more than we know.
items.Critics argue that constant connectivity: 'Eroding' means slowly destroying. Critics say being online all the time hurts our focus.
items.Online privacy is something most people: 'Take for granted' means not value until you lose it. People don't think about privacy until it's gone.
items.The new regulations are a step in the ri: 'A step in the right direction' means good progress. But the new rules are still not strong enough.
items.People tend to overestimate how much oth: 'Overestimate' means think something is bigger than it is. We think people see our mistakes more than they do.
items.He's quick to criticise others, yet he c: He criticizes people fast, but he gets upset when others criticize him.
items.Procrastination is often less about lazi: 'Procrastination' means delaying things. It often comes from being afraid to fail, not from being lazy.
items.If I'd slept better last night, I wouldn: 'Irritable' means easily angry. If I slept well, I wouldn't feel so angry now.
items.She tends to bottle up her feelings unti: 'Bottle up' means keep feelings inside. 'Snaps' means suddenly gets angry.
items.We're far more likely to stick to a habi: 'Stick to a habit' means keep doing it. Writing down your progress helps.
items.Unless we act now, rising temperatures w: 'Unless we act now' means if we don't do something now. Hotter weather will hurt poor people most.
items.Recycling alone won't solve the problem;: Recycling is not enough; we must buy and use much less.
items.The company was accused of greenwashing: 'Greenwashing' means pretending to be good for nature. The company said it did more than it did.
items.Solar energy makes perfect sense in a co: 'Makes perfect sense' means is very logical. Israel has lots of sun, so sun power is smart.
items.It's estimated that the city will face s: 'It's estimated' means people guess. The city may not have enough water in 20 years.
items.Little did we realise how quickly the co: 'Little did we realise' means we didn't know at all. The beach changed fast in our lives.
items.The film received rave reviews, but I fo: 'Rave reviews' means very good opinions. 'Predictable' means you know what will happen. I found it boring.
items.Public funding for the arts is often the: When there is a crisis, the government often stops giving money to art first.
items.Her latest exhibition really struck a ch: 'Struck a chord' means made people feel something. Young visitors loved her new show.
items.I'm not much of a theatre buff, but that: A 'theatre buff' loves theatre. 'Blew me away' means I was amazed.
items.Some critics claim that streaming has lo: Some critics say watching TV online made shows worse, but I don't think so.
items.The novel is said to have been inspired: 'Is said to have been inspired' means people say the idea came from the writer's early life in Jaffa.
items.I'd argue productivity depends more on m: 'Outperform' means do better than. Good managers matter more than place; some home teams work better.
items.That's a bit sweeping; it certainly has: 'Sweeping' means too general. It has bad sides, but it also connects people and shares news.
items.Experience is invaluable, but for some p: 'Invaluable' means very valuable. Experience is great, but doctors and engineers really need a degree.
items.Banning it outright seems extreme; smart: 'Banning it outright' means stopping it completely. Better rules could help people and shops.
items.I'm not so sure; history suggests techno: 'Transforms' means changes. In the past, technology changed jobs, so we must be ready to learn new skills.
items.Every generation says that, though; kids: 'Resilient' means strong after hard times. Kids today have different problems and are very strong.
items.The subsequent experiments confirmed the: Subsequent = coming later. Later experiments showed the 2019 study's results were correct.
items.A considerable number of participants wi: Considerable = large. Many people left the study before it ended.
items.Some economists believe that a period of: Inevitable = sure to happen. Some economists think slower growth will almost surely come.
items.Repeated budget cuts may seriously under: Undermine = make weaker. Cutting money again and again can hurt public schools.
items.The report provides a comprehensive revi: Comprehensive = complete, covering everything. The report looks at all research on children's food.
items.Many English words derive from Latin, ei: Derive from = come from. Many English words come from Latin, sometimes through French.
items.Fresh water is becoming increasingly sca: Scarce = hard to find, not enough. There is less and less fresh water in the Middle East.
items.The effect of the medication tends to di: Diminish = become smaller. The medicine usually works less after a few weeks.
items.Historians attribute the decline of the: Attribute to = say something was caused by. Historians say money problems made the empire weaker.
items.Solar energy has become a viable alterna: Viable = can work well. In sunny countries, solar energy can really replace coal.
items.Vitamin D deficiency is surprisingly pre: Prevalent = common; deficiency = not enough. Many people lack vitamin D, even in sunny places.
items.The notion that intelligence is fixed at: Notion = idea. Most researchers say intelligence is not fixed when you are born.
items.The theory was widely criticized; nevert: Nevertheless = but still. Many criticized the theory, but it still influenced research for years.
items.Whereas the first group improved steadil: Whereas = while (shows contrast). The first group got better; the second group did not.
items.Despite the high cost of the treatment,: Despite = even with. The treatment was expensive, but many patients continued it.
items.Although the sample was small, the findi: Although = even though. The study was small, but the results matched older studies.
items.Urban residents earn more on average; co: Conversely = on the opposite side. City people earn more, but living there costs much more.
items.The method is fast and cheap; on the oth: On the other hand = shows the opposite point. The method is quick and cheap, but sometimes wrong.
items.The factory was closed due to repeated v: Due to = because of. The factory closed because it broke environment rules many times.
items.Rising sea temperatures have given rise: Give rise to = cause. Warmer seas cause more and stronger storms.
items.Many health problems in old age stem fro: Stem from = come from, be caused by. Habits from young adulthood cause many health problems later.
items.The drug had serious side effects; conse: Consequently = as a result. The drug was dangerous, so it was taken off the market.
items.The data were incomplete, and the conclu: Thus = so, therefore. The data were missing parts, so the conclusions may be wrong.
items.Prices rose sharply during the drought;: Hence = so, for this reason. Prices went up a lot, so families bought less food.
items.Not until the late nineteenth century di: Not until = only at that time. Scientists first understood how diseases spread in the late 1800s.
items.Hardly any of the original documents sur: Hardly any = almost none. Almost all the old documents burned in the fire.
items.The bridge was designed by an engineer w: The engineer who planned the bridge had never built anything so big before.
items.It is unlikely that the new policy will: Unlikely = probably not. The new policy probably won't change the number of people without jobs.
items.Few researchers would dispute the claim: Dispute = argue against. Almost all researchers agree smoking makes cancer more likely.
items.The more people use public transport, th: "The more... the less" = one grows, the other shrinks. More buses and trains mean fewer cars.
items.The results suggest that regular exercis: Suggest / may = maybe, not sure. Exercise might help memory loss happen more slowly.
items.Arguably, the printing press had a great: Arguably = you can give reasons for this. Maybe printing changed society more than the internet.
items.People tend to overestimate the risk of: Overestimate = think something is bigger than it is. People think rare dangers are more likely than they are.
items.It is widely believed that the city was: Widely believed = many people think. Many think traders from the coast started the city.
items.Many scientists remain skeptical of clai: Skeptical = not believing, doubting. Many scientists doubt the treatment really cures the disease.
items.The evidence, while promising, is not ye: Promising = looks good; justify = give a good reason for. The evidence looks good but isn't enough yet.
items.In the opening paragraph, the author pre: Rejects = says no to. First the writer shows a popular idea, then later says it is wrong.
items.The main purpose of the passage is to co: Purpose = reason, goal. The text mainly compares two ways to treat depression.
items.The word it in the second sentence refer: Refers to = points to, means. In sentence two, "it" means the government's new tax plan.
items.The passage implies that the experiment: Implies = says without saying directly. The text hints the experiment needed more money to succeed.
items.The final paragraph summarizes the argum: Summarizes = says the main points shortly. The last paragraph repeats the main ideas and suggests next research.
items.The example of the honeybee is given to: Illustrate = show with an example. The honeybee example shows how animals share information.
items.Read the whole sentence before choosing: Since = because. Read all the sentence first, because the important hint may be at the end.
items.Pay close attention to connectors like a: Signal = show. Words like although and therefore show how ideas in a sentence connect.
items.In restatement questions, reject any opt: Restatement = saying the same idea in other words. Don't choose answers that change the meaning even a little.
items.Read the questions before the passage so: So that = in order to. Read the questions first, so you know what to look for.
items.If a question seems too difficult, skip: Skip = jump over. If a question is too hard, leave it and come back later.
items.Words like always and never often indica: Indicate = show; extreme = too strong. Answers with always or never are often wrong.

Itay and Omer are best friends who had a fight about football. After three days, Omer said sorry. Now they are friends again and plan a bike trip.
Yael is thirteen and does judo three times a week. In her first competition she lost once and won twice. Her coach is proud of her.
Daniel makes short cooking videos on YouTube every Friday. Now two thousand people watch him. He ignores mean comments, and school is still first for him.
Tamar was always tired at school because she slept late and skipped breakfast. Now she sleeps early and eats a good breakfast. She feels much better.
m8: Roni loves computers and is in a robot club. Her team built a robot that sorts plastic and paper. It broke, but they fixed it for a big competition.
Eitan's class cleaned a dirty beach for three hours and filled forty bags with garbage. Now Eitan uses a metal bottle so he won't need plastic ones.
Shira plays piano and now writes her own songs. At a show her microphone stopped, but she kept singing louder. Everyone clapped.
Lior's family went to London for a week. When it rained, they went into a cafe and drank English tea. He saw many red buses and wants to visit Scotland next.
Ariel felt sick during a race because he didn't drink enough water. The doctor told him to drink more and eat breakfast. Now he runs with no problems.
m9: Gal, a ninth grader, helps old people at a center. At first she was nervous, but she became close to Rivka, who told her many stories. Now Gal sees old people differently.
Yonatan's class visited a tech company. Many workers there had other jobs before, like Dana, who was a dancer. Her advice: never stop learning.
Masada is a famous old place on a high mountain near the Dead Sea. Many people climb it early to see the sun come up. Adi's class did it and loved the view.
Noam's grandfather wrote letters and waited weeks for answers; now messages are instant. Noam thinks the future will have electric cars and robots. But he hopes people will still talk face to face.
A fake photo of a shark on a road was shared a lot. Michal checked it online and found it was changed. Now her classmates check stories before sharing.
h10: Noa used her phone six hours a day, and she was tired and her grades went down. She stopped using it after 9 p.m. Now she sleeps better, reads more and feels in control.
People leave plastic on Israeli beaches, and it hurts sea turtles. Students in Ashdod began cleaning their beach every Friday, and many joined them. The city added recycling bins.
A video of a big shark near Tel Aviv was shared by many people. A journalist found it was changed and filmed in Australia. Always ask who made something and why.
Omer drank many energy drinks to study, but got headaches and couldn't sleep. His doctor told him to drink water and walk instead. Soon he slept well and his grades got better.
Israeli students must help in the community for sixty hours. Tamar helped children with special needs and loved it. She kept going after her hours and may study special education.
h11: Many Israeli schools now use AI tools that help each student learn at their own speed. Some worry students won't learn to think alone, and AI can be wrong. Teachers say: teach students to use it carefully.
Israel once had too little water, so it invented drip watering and built plants that make sea water drinkable. But this uses lots of energy. Now scientists want to use clean energy for it.
In 2019, a small Israeli spaceship called Beresheet tried to land on the Moon but crashed. Still, many saw it as a big success. It made many children want to study science.
Masada is an old fort on a high rock near the Dead Sea. A story says Jewish fighters there chose to die rather than become Roman slaves. Some experts doubt parts of the story.
A study asked Israeli teens what matters most in a job. Most said work with meaning and a good life balance, not money. Experts say this may change when they must pay rent.
h12: A car with no driver may have to choose who gets hurt in a crash. People from different places answer this question differently. No one agrees yet on who should decide.

About one third of all food in the world is thrown away, while many people are hungry. Groups like Leket Israel give extra food to poor families. Experts say we must also change how we buy and use food.
Many Israelis start university late, after the army and travel. Some say this is bad because they start work later. Others say older students are more serious and know what they want.
Eurovision is a big song contest, and Israel has won it four times. Some say the votes are about politics, not music. Still, it lets the world hear Hebrew songs.
Many people today feel lonely, even though they are connected online. Loneliness is very bad for health, for young and old. Programs that bring people together face to face can help.
uni: To understand a text well, you must know almost all of its words. University texts use many words that people do not say every day. So it helps to learn a list of common academic words early.

A study asked 240 Israeli students about phone use and sleep. Students who used their phones in bed slept about 40 minutes less and found it harder to focus in class. Universities should teach students about good sleep habits.
A student writes a polite email to her professor. She asks to hand in her final paper one week late because she was in the hospital. She adds a doctor's note and thanks him.

A good class talk starts by saying the topic and the plan. Slides should have only a few points, and the speaker should look at people and speak slowly. End with a short summary and be ready for questions.
Academic writers do not say things are 100% sure. They use soft words like 'may' and 'might' to be careful. Linking words like 'however' help readers follow the ideas.
A chart shows how many foreign students came to an Israeli university from 2018 to 2024. The number went up, fell in 2021 because of travel limits, then went up again to 1,400. In general it grew.
Many Israeli students take an English reading test. Read the questions first, find the main idea of each paragraph, and guess new words from the text around them. Practice with a timer.

The train to the airport leaves at 9:30 and takes forty minutes. A ticket is fifteen dollars, and you buy it at a machine.
adv: Tamar found a nice apartment but read the contract first. Two parts were unfair to her, so she talked with the owner politely. He agreed to change them, and she saved money and stress.
A couple did not check their bank papers for years. Their daughter found high fees, little interest and a minus account. They met the bank, got lower fees and started saving each month.

Ronit's new washing machine leaked, and no one took responsibility. She kept careful notes and wrote a calm, clear email asking for a new machine or her money back. The company quickly sent her a new one.
Ofer went to a party where he knew almost no one. He asked people simple questions and listened, and he made a joke when politics came up. He made new friends who helped him at his new job.
Yael waited a long time to treat her knee pain. She found an early appointment and wrote her symptoms before going. The doctor said it was a small injury and sent her to physiotherapy.
A video of a store throwing away vegetables went viral, and people got angry. Reporters found it was old and from another country. Experts say: stop and check the date and source before sharing.
Nadia moved and had many problems with the city tax and her insurance. A neighbor told her to get names, ask for promises in writing and complain formally. Then things moved faster and were fixed.
biz: Daniel writes to a woman he heard speak at a conference. He tells her that his company's results support her idea about helping customers sign up. He politely asks for a short call to hear her advice.
Noa sends a summary of a team meeting. The warehouse move will happen two weeks later, and the team will test a new delivery company. The meeting was too long, so next time she will plan time better.
Michal writes a polite reminder that a customer has not paid a bill. She says it may be a mistake and offers help. She asks for an answer by Friday, or the finance team will take the next steps.

HR says people like working from home, but they feel far from each other. So teams will come to the office two days a week. There are also new rules for video calls, and special cases can be discussed.
Eitan says the app can't be ready on time because the payment part must be rebuilt. He suggests launching in mid-May instead. He asks to meet the marketing team about the change.
A big client wanted to leave for a cheaper supplier. The manager learned the real problem was late deliveries, not price. She fixed the delivery problem, and the client stayed and ordered more.
Sales grew 7% but missed the goal, mostly because electronics sales fell. Sports products grew a lot, and more customers came back. The team will move money to the strong areas.
A company says sorry to a customer whose table arrived broken. It says the damage was not her fault. It will bring a new table for free and return the delivery money.
A company can't cut its price by 12%. Instead it offers 7% off if the client signs for three years. It also suggests fewer deliveries to save money for both sides.
pro: The writer used to think idioms were not important. Then he saw fluent speakers miss the meaning of an idiom at dinner. Now he thinks idioms help you really be part of a conversation, but you should learn them naturally.
Noa saw that tasks were forgotten at her company. She sent short notes after meetings and friendly reminders. Missed deadlines fell by half, which shows that following up turns ideas into results.
People often think changing your mind is weak. The writer says it is good to change your opinion when new facts appear. But you should not change it just because someone is loud.

People argue whether social media is good or bad. The writer says phones are not neutral tools: they are built to keep us using them. But they also help, so we must ask who designs them and what rules they need.

The 'spotlight effect' means we think others notice our mistakes much more than they do. In one study, people guessed half the room saw their shirt, but less than a quarter did. Knowing this can help us feel freer.

Some people think technology will save us; others think it's too late. The writer says both ideas stop us from acting. Israel's water success shows that hard work and investment can make a real difference.
The writer laughed at a chair shown as art in a gallery. But it started a long, deep talk, so he changed his mind a little. He thinks we should be open to new art but still ask hard questions.
amir: Cities are hotter than the countryside because roads and roofs keep the sun's heat and there are few trees. This uses more energy and is dangerous for health. White roofs, parks and trees can help cool cities.

Almost half of the world's languages may disappear soon, because young people move to cities and use big languages. Every language has special knowledge and ways of thinking. Hebrew shows a language can come back, but this is hard.

Many students don't sleep before exams, but this is a bad idea. During sleep, the brain keeps what we learned, and tired students make more mistakes. It is better to study over several days and sleep well.

Trees put water into the air, and this helps make rain far away. When people cut forests for farms, roads or mining, there is less rain. So the farmers themselves can be hurt, and saving forests is good for the economy too.

People once thought learning two languages confuses children. Those old studies were bad, and better studies showed no real problem. Bilingual children know as many words in total, and mixing languages is normal.

News about coffee often changes, because most studies only show connections, not causes. Today, three to four cups a day seem safe and maybe a little healthy. But pregnant women and sensitive people should drink less.

In citizen science, ordinary volunteers help scientists collect information, like counting birds or sorting photos of space. Some worry the data is not exact, but checking methods make it almost as good as experts' data. Volunteers also become more interested in science.
Reading notes again is not a good way to study. Testing yourself helps you remember much more and shows what you don't know. For an exam, practice with questions over several weeks.
